newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply lower after funds sell.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply lower after funds sell.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply lower as funds sold heavily, taking profits despite a healthy drawdown in London Metal Exchange stocks.
Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said the funds sold-off and took profits due to disappointment that the market could not decisively stay above 90 cents per pound.
"The draw down on LME was quite constructive, but the market was hoping for higher numbers," Raptopoulos said.
LME stocks fell 7,825 tonnes to 239,500 tonnes.
December COMEX settled 2.25 cents weaker at 87.85 cents per pound, traded 89.20 to 87.60 cents.
Traders said there was no fundamental news to prompt the fall with business was still good in the United States.

"It seems the funds really ganged up on this market and wanted to push their winnings further and sold it," a COMEX and LME broker said. "The funds were on the short side and seem to be running the show - there is no opposition, no Hamanaka!"

A joint statement issued late Monday from Kennecott Copper in Utah and the labor unions said there would be no strike at the refinery after a failure to reach a new pay deal by midnight local time when the previous contract expired.
